text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Netanyahu: We will not accept U.S. dictates.
- Report handed to defence minister points to sharp erosion in Israeli readiness for war.
- The soldier who fired in Hebron market free to wander streets of Jerusalem.
- Israeli contractor building at Jewish enclave in Hebron stole equipment from American project to refurbish Arab street.
JERUSALEM POST
- Legislators, army chief: budget cuts hurting army's readiness.
- U.S. envoy Ross due tomorrow.
- Attacker who stabbed soldier shot to death.
- Palestinian probe: sack ministers.
- Finance minister: government to promote long-term investment.
- Industry ministry to undergo overhaul.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Cabinet minister Sharansky questioned over links with suspect Gregory Lerner.
- Report in Janes Intelligence Review says Israeli nuclear weapons exposed to attack.
MAARIV
- Pro-Israel lobby in Washington trying to convince U.S. to alter its initiative for reviving peacemaking.
- Report confirms Yarkon river where bridge collapsed contains dangerous toxins.
GLOBES
- Electric company says process of choosing Lehman Brothers for bond issue was proper.
- Ehud Eliav removed from Electric Company's board of directors over possible conflict of interests.
